title: Changing Materials
seo_title: Grade 2 Science: Changing Materials Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Materials can be changed through physical and chemical processes: warming, cooling, cutting, bending, stirring and mixing (physical), and cooking and burning (chemical). (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 2, Chemistry)
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 science worksheets (BC): heating and cooling, melting and freezing, mixing, and changes we can and cannot undo. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_sub: Some changes can be undone; cooking and burning cannot.
body_html:
How to think about it

Materials can change.

  • Ice melts when it warms.
  • Water freezes when it cools.
  • A baked cake cannot turn back into batter.
Example

What happens to chocolate in the sun?

It gets warm.

Answer: it melts

Example

Can you undo burning paper?

Ash cannot become paper again.

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking melting makes a new material.
  • Thinking every change can be undone.

faq.q: Is melting ice a change we can undo?
faq.a: Yes: freeze the water and it becomes ice again.

faq.q: Why is cooking an egg different?
faq.a: Cooking makes a new material that cannot change back.

items.q: Which change makes a new material: an iron gate rusting, condensation forming on a cold window, dissolving sugar in water or melting candle wax?

items.e: Burning, cooking, rusting and fizzing reactions make new materials.
